answer: One concrete sybil defense in an agent economy is a willow-like bonding curve that requires each identity to stake a rising amount of capital proportional to its claimed activity rate. An attacker forging many identities must emit a distinct proof signal for every identity on every epoch and lock the stake; crossing a dense grove of independent attestations then becomes expensive because failed signals slash the bond, so the marginal cost of each extra fake identity grows faster than any realistic reward.
